 MAYVILLE — The Mayville Schools Board of Education met on Wednesday November 11, 2026, discussing the monthly updates for the district and other matters.
 The Mayville Schools Board of Education discussed business ranging from grant spending, personnel and possible FAFSA Challenge Grant participation at the Nov. 11 meeting.
 Courtesy photo | The Advertiser
 The meeting began with the recognition of the students of the month. First up the students of the month for fourth grade were Layla Stephens, Logan Berlin, Camry Berry and Leland Howell. The students of the month for the middle and high school were Alizabeth Epley and Austin Putnam. Isabella West was also honored as student of the month for October, having been unable to attend that meeting.
 Moving on to the first reports of the night, beginning with the athletics report. Superintendent Seaman told the board that the middle and high school gym floor would be rewaxed over the Thanksgiving holiday. The new scoreboard for the middle and high school were delivered on Nov. 11 and plans were started to have them start being put up on Nov. 12. It was also said that they were going to have plaques put in under the scoreboards. Seaman also acknowledged the cross country state finalists from Mayville and the all conference students for football and volleyball.
 Moving on to the food services it was said that the district was looking for a sub for the kitchens and they had someone in mind from the Caro area. The 10 Cent Grant was renamed the Good Food for Michigan Grant and they are working on getting suppliers for Michigan made foods and that the health department did their annual inspection at the end of October. For the transportation update it was said that there was an update on the bus inspections and two older buses need some work and they would be reinspected later. A heating pipe in the high school cracked and was also repaired.
 Melodie Howes shakes the hands of the Mayville Schoolboard after being honored for her work at the November board meeting.
 Courtesy photo | The Advertiser
 The reports for the middle and high school and the elementary school were both given by Middle and High School Principal Jenna Tetil. For the middle and high school Tetil talked about building foundations for students and Portrait of a Wildcat. She said they started the year by introducing the MTSS framework and that round two of meetings. She also talked about Halloween Week and the PSAT and NMSQT practice testing in October. The NHS hosted a blood drive. She also talked about the Wildcat Big Buddy program. Top of the Pack was brought up with 90 students qualifying for the first term reward, and over 30 kids had perfect attendance. Tetil also fielded a question about the PBIS behavioral management process.
 After the middle and high school report Tetil also went over the elementary report in the absence of Elementary Principal Cheryl Rayl. She talked about how parent teacher conferences on October 15 went, and that there was parent participation for 96 percent of kids. The book fair was the same week as parent teacher conferences and the school earned $1,640 for new library materials. Tetil also spoke about teachers participating in a virtual MTSS professional development session. The Halloween festivities for the school were a success and it was announced that Mayville Elementary was in the top 40 percent of elementary schools in Michigan for the 2027 USA News and World Report 2027 Best Elementary Schools rankings.
 The last report was the superintendent report from Superintendent Seaman. He also spoke about parent teacher conferences and PIE Night, which was scheduled for November 12. The procedures for snow days and delays were talked about, which will remain relatively the same. Seaman spoke about school board elections and said that they need to be finalized by the county. The new board will take office in January. He also said that the admin team went to training at the ISD on Nov. 2. Seaman also said he would like to have a strategic planning meeting for the community on December 17 in the old high school media center. There was an update on the 12E grant and gave a staff shout out to Melodie Howes, who teaches Spanish and also oversees the state testing and the National Honor Society.
 After the reports the meeting was opened for public comment with no one participating. The board then approved the consent agenda which included previous meeting minutes and payment of the bills. For correspondence there was a thank you to Michael and Sharon Venia to the cross country team, and a thank you to Madison Franzel and McDonald Chevrolet for donating a vehicle for the cross county team to take to the state championships.
 Moving on to personnel the board approved second year probation for Mallory Ruggles, Ruggles oversees the GSRP program for the district. They also approved hiring Courtney Flanagan as varsity girls basketball coach, and Joe Russell as the junior varsity girls basketball coach. There were two resignations as well. Missy LaBean resigned as a cook effective on January 15, 2027 and Rynae Epley resigned as a paraprofessional for the elementary school.
 Next up came the new business which started with the approval of buying new copy paper. The board approved the purchase of 320 cases of paper from CPG, which totaled $10,592. The district chose to buy the paper before the end of the year to avoid an upcoming price increase they were informed of. They also approved the recommendation by Chip Hendrick to use Buchinger Roofing for the work on the middle and high school roof and central office roof. The projects will be funded through the 12E grant.
 Tetil once again spoke to the board about the FAFSA Challenge Grant. She explained to the board that the district would get grant money if they made completing the FAFSA a graduation requirement, and answered questions from the board about what happens if not all students complete it. Tetil explained that there were waivers for families that are paying for college another way and exemptions as well, so the district is protected. The board gave their support for moving forward with exploring the grant.
 Finally in the other matters of the board they discussed PIE Night and the Fall School Board Dinner at the Tuscola ISD on Nov. 17.
 After the other matters of the board the meeting was adjourned.
